indication: [AGE]-year-old [GENDER] presenting with constipation. Evaluate for bowel obstruction or other intra-abdominal pathology.
technique: ** Helical CT imaging was performed from the diaphragm through the symphysis pubis following the administration of intravenous contrast. Multiplanar reformats were reviewed.
findings:
**
The liver demonstrates normal size and contour without focal mass or intrahepatic biliary ductal dilatation. The gallbladder is present without wall thickening or pericholecystic fluid. The spleen and pancreas are unremarkable in appearance. The adrenal glands are symmetric and within normal limits for age.
Regarding the gastrointestinal tract, there is no evidence of high-grade mechanical bowel obstruction. There is mild fecal loading throughout the colon, consistent with the clinical history of constipation, but no transition point or abnormal bowel wall thickening is identified. The appendix is visualized and appears normal.
The kidneys show symmetric enhancement and excretion of contrast without hydronephrosis. The urinary bladder is partially filled and has smooth walls. No free intraperitoneal air or significant ascites is noted. The visualized pelvic organs are unremarkable.
Within the visualized musculoskeletal system, there is an aggressive lytic lesion involving the L2 vertebral body. This lesion is associated with significant cortical thinning of the anterior and lateral margins, which puts the segment at increased risk for pathologic collapse. There is mild degenerative disc disease seen at L4-L5 and L5-S1 with small marginal osteophytes. A few small, benign-appearing sclerotic islands are noted in the right iliac wing.
conclusion:
**
Lytic lesion in the L2 vertebral body with associated cortical thinning and risk of vertebral collapse. No associated spinal canal compromise is seen at this time.
